title: Round 28 Missouri-Arkansas state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Missouri and Arkansas. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Taum Sauk Mountain and Magazine Mountain additionally carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks. Magazine Mountain is the series' first Ridge-class row.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. County divisions, bends, levees, planning regions, historical places, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Taum Sauk Mountain (752501) and Magazine Mountain (67051), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the two high-point elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-11; this register is the frozen batch-11 evidence. Extract county spellings are preserved verbatim ('St. Charles', 'St. Louis (city)') and normalized in verification rather than edited.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

A row is additionally rejected when the agreed GNIS point itself is geographically impossible for the named feature (the round-27 Indian Lake lesson); two-surface agreement is necessary but not sufficient evidence.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes and reservoirs (the extract's text class for all six batch-11 lake rows is Reservoir), Streams & Canals to Stream, Summit to Summit, and Ridge to Ridge (Magazine Mountain; the gazetteer gained a Ridge class entry for this batch).
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit/ridge outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

missouri.title: Missouri statewide frame (Missouri-Arkansas batch)

identityDecisions.candidate: Magazine Mountain, FEATURE_ID 67051 — GNIS class Ridge, not Summit
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded as the series' first Ridge-class row. Both USGS surfaces classify the Logan County mesa as Ridge (the state-highpoint summit is Signal Hill on its crest); the gazetteer gained a Ridge entry (js/city-gazetteer.js GAZ_CLASS_META, path phys.ridge) rather than misnaming the class Summit. The 2,753-foot elevation cites USGS-published state-highpoint values.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a surveyed summit outline, ridge line, or trailhead geocode.

knownLimitations: Missouri and Arkansas are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Taum Sauk Mountain (1,772 feet) and Magazine Mountain (2,753 feet) elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values; GNIS identity rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include areas outside their state outlines; no boundary geometry is claimed.
